project.name: pre-cr-suite-lsp
project.identity: A coverage-first pre-PR readiness tool for VS Code and Neovim with a shared configuration workflow across editor and headless use.
project.audience: Developers who want repository checks and readiness evidence before opening a code review, whether working in an editor or headless environment.
project.core_loop: Load repository configuration, run supported readiness checks, show coverage and failures, fix or review the result, and use the same evidence before a pull request.
project.north_star: A developer sees the important pre-PR risks early through the same inspectable workflow in the editor and headless environments.
not_this: A silent auto-fixer that hides failed checks
An editor-only feature with no headless parity

mvp.definition: The tool runs the supported pre-PR checks from one configuration in VS Code, Neovim, and headless mode with clear coverage and failure output.

complete_product.definition: The suite provides reliable, coverage-first pre-PR readiness across supported editors and headless workflows with shared configuration, actionable failures, and release-quality compatibility.

outcomes.name: Supported checks and their coverage are visible before a pull request, regardless of the supported client surface.

layers.intended: Developers understand what was checked and what was not before review.
layers.planned: The beta promise centres one configuration across VS Code, Neovim, and headless use.
layers.implemented: The repository provides the LSP and pre-PR readiness surface.
layers.verified: Repository docs establish the promise; editor/headless compatibility was not rerun here.

evidence.note: Defines coverage-first pre-PR readiness and the editor/headless beta promise.
Provides repository context and workflow boundaries.

blockers.summary: Supported editor, headless, and representative repository coverage needs executable compatibility evidence.

outcomes.name: A readiness run distinguishes passed, failed, skipped, unavailable, and out-of-scope checks with a next safe action.

layers.intended: A failed gate helps the developer decide what to fix or review rather than appearing as unexplained noise.
layers.planned: The project describes coverage-first and cross-surface operation.
layers.implemented: The repository contains the readiness tool and client integration surfaces.
